We exist to wow our customers. We know we’re doing the right thing when we hear our customers say, “How did I ever live without Coupang?” Born out of an obsession to make shopping, eating, and living easier than ever, we’re collectively disrupting the multi-billion-dollar commerce industry from the ground up. At our core, we are bold and ambitious people that like to get our hands dirty and make a hands-on impact. At Coupang, you will see yourself, your colleagues, your team, and the company grow every day.
Our mission to build the future of commerce is real. We push the boundaries of what’s possible to solve problems and break traditional tradeoffs. Join Coupang now to create an epic experience in this always-on, high-tech, and hyper-connected world.
Role Overview
Coupang is seeking a highly technical and execution-focused Staff Technical Program Manager to lead Engineering Controls, Operational Governance, IT SOX Compliance, Security, Privacy and Technology Risk initiatives across Coupang's technology ecosystem.
This role sits at the intersection of software engineering, DevOps, cloud infrastructure, operational excellence, compliance, and AI-enabled governance. The primary focus is ownership of IT SOX Change Management controls and serving as a Second Line of Defense (2LOD) partner to engineering teams by independently assessing control effectiveness, monitoring software deployment activities, identifying compliance risks, and driving scalable engineering controls.
As Coupang continues to evolve its engineering platform, this role will help modernize compliance through automation, analytics, engineering telemetry, and AI-driven monitoring. The TPM will build a control environment that improves risk visibility, audit readiness, and operational excellence while minimizing compliance friction for engineering teams.
Unlike traditional audit or compliance roles, this position requires deep expertise in modern software development, CI/CD, release management, cloud-native architectures, deployment automation, and engineering operations. The ideal candidate is a former Software Engineer, Platform Engineer, DevOps Engineer, or SRE who has transitioned into technical program leadership and can effectively partner with engineers, architects, security leaders, auditors, and executives.
You will work closely with Engineering, Platform, Security, Privacy, Finance, Internal Audit, and Governance teams to strengthen controls, automate compliance processes, improve reliability, and enable rapid software delivery without compromising risk objectives.
What You Will Do
Lead Change Management Governance
Own the strategy, governance framework, and roadmap for IT SOX Change Management controls across Coupang's software development lifecycle.
Evaluate release processes, CI/CD pipelines, and production deployments to ensure compliance requirements are consistently met.
Perform independent monitoring and oversight of deployment activities using engineering and compliance data.
Identify compliance exceptions, unauthorized changes, control failures, and process gaps through continuous monitoring.
Establish and improve controls related to:
Code Reviews
Release Approvals
Segregation of Duties (SoD)
Emergency Changes
Production Deployments
Change Monitoring and Reporting
Leverage AI, analytics, and deployment telemetry to identify elevated-risk changes, anomalous deployment patterns, and control exceptions.
Provide guidance to engineering teams and drive remediation of identified risks and control gaps.
Balance engineering velocity with effective risk management through automation and scalable controls.
Drive CI/CD Governance & Engineering Controls
Partner with Platform Engineering teams to embed preventive and detective controls directly into software delivery workflows.
Improve governance across CI/CD, release management, deployment authorization, and production change processes.
Define control observability frameworks that provide real-time visibility into software delivery controls.
Partner with Platform and Data teams to develop automated monitoring capabilities that detect unauthorized changes, control bypasses, deployment anomalies, and emerging risks.
Establish key control and risk indicators that proactively surface compliance concerns.
Design monitoring and reporting solutions for:
Release Compliance
Deployment Risk
Control Effectiveness
SoD Violations
Emergency Changes
Change Failure Trends
Develop metrics and dashboards that provide visibility into compliance, operational performance, and risk posture.
Promote automation-first approaches to evidence generation, control testing, and compliance assurance.
Security, Privacy & Technology Risk
Partner with Security, Privacy, and Risk organizations to align engineering controls with enterprise requirements and regulatory obligations.
Support technology risk assessments, regulatory reviews, and remediation programs.
Drive consistent implementation of security, privacy, and risk controls across engineering organizations.
Promote secure-by-design and privacy-by-design principles within software delivery processes.
Lead Audit Readiness & Continuous Assurance
Own evidence collection processes supporting SOX audits and compliance reviews.
Establish automated and repeatable evidence collection mechanisms that improve audit readiness and reduce manual effort.
Lead walkthroughs with Internal and External Audit teams.
Serve as the primary technical SME during audit engagements.
Validate the completeness and accuracy of audit evidence and management responses.
Establish continuous assurance capabilities through automated monitoring and risk-based assessments.
Drive timely resolution of audit findings, control deficiencies, and remediation actions.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical field.
10+ years of experience in Software Engineering, Technical Program Management, Platform Engineering, DevOps, SRE, or related technical leadership roles.
5+ years of experience leading large-scale cross-functional technical programs.
Previous hands-on experience as a Software Engineer, Platform Engineer, Infrastructure Engineer, SRE, DevOps Engineer, or equivalent technical role.
Experience operating in modern cloud-native software development environments.
Experience supporting SOX, ITGC, Change Management, Security, Privacy, or Technology Risk programs.
Experience partnering with engineering organizations responsible for enterprise-scale software delivery.
Strong program management, stakeholder management, and executive communication skills.
Preferred Qualifications
Deep expertise in modern software engineering practices, including SDLC, CI/CD, release management, change management, and platform engineering.
Strong experience with cloud-native architectures, Infrastructure as Code (IaC), site reliability engineering (SRE), and large-scale production operations.
Hands-on experience with DevOps and deployment technologies such as GitHub Actions, Jenkins, ArgoCD, Spinnaker, Azure DevOps, Kubernetes, and Terraform.
Proficiency in public cloud platforms, including AWS, Azure, or GCP.
Experience leveraging data analytics, observability, and automation to improve engineering performance, operational excellence, and risk visibility.
Demonstrated ability to design and implement AI-enabled compliance solutions, including continuous control monitoring, automated evidence collection, and risk analysis.
Working knowledge of SOX, ITGCs, change and access management controls, segregation of duties (SoD), and industry frameworks such as COBIT, COSO, NIST, and ISO 27001.

Dazu gehören geplante präventive Wartungsarbeiten an Geräten, tägliche Korrekturarbeiten und die Notfallreaktion auf akute Probleme. Du fungierst als technischer Experte und berichtest an den Data Center Facility Manager vor Ort. Gleichzeitig arbeitest du mit den Engineering Operations Technicians (EOT) vor Ort sowie mit externen Dienstleistern zusammen. Als zentrale Anlaufstelle für alle Betriebsabläufe in einem bestimmten Rechenzentrum unterstützt du Amazon in den eigenen und betriebenen Rechenzentren. Die Ausrüstung der Rechenzentren, die missionskritische Server unterstützt, muss eine Verfügbarkeit von mehr als 99,999 % gewährleisten. Als DCEO Chief Engineer leitest du Projekte mit geringem bis mittlerem Einfluss von der Konzeption bis zur Fertigstellung. Zudem wird die Umsetzung und Durchführung standort- und gerätespezifischer Schulungsmaßnahmen erwartet. Scale builds enterprise AI systems deployed into production. As a Staff Solutions Architect, you lead technical execution on the most complex and highest-value enterprise opportunities in your vertical, and you set the technical standard the rest of the team works to.
You own an assigned set of strategic accounts and remain the senior technical relationship owner across them. Most complex opportunities.
Lead technical strategy and execution on the largest and most complex deals in your vertical, measured by revenue, product scope, or data volume. Act as the final technical authority on whether Scale can deliver what is being proposed.

Own qualification on ambiguous, multi-stakeholder opportunities where requirements are unresolved. Make and defend go/no-go and disqualification recommendations on deals with significant revenue attached.

Executive technical relationships.

Lead workshops, technical deep dives, and executive presentations on strategic opportunities. Build or direct the prototypes that make complex solutions tangible.
Technical standards and reusable solution patterns.
Build reference architectures, demo environments, discovery patterns, and solution blueprints that become standard practice across the team. Where appropriate, drive solutions that graduate into Scale's product and solution stack.
Technical sales process.
Create or change the technical processes the team runs on, including qualification standards, workshop practice, and scoping approach. Drive initiatives that improve win rates, shorten cycles, or increase the scalability of the Solutions Architecture function.
Product roadmap influence.
Synthesize patterns across accounts into prioritized, evidence-backed input to Product and Engineering. Contribute to strategic roadmap decisions rather than submitting individual feature requests.
Mentorship and technical bar-raising.
Mentor other Solutions Architects, raise the technical standard across the team, and serve on hiring panels. Document and distribute what you learn so it does not have to be relearned.

Deep engineering background with substantial experience in customer-facing technical roles at enterprise scale: solutions architecture, sales engineering, forward-deployed engineering, or technical consulting. Hands-on proficiency in Python or equivalent language.

Strong systems thinking across cloud, data, and AI/ML architecture, with production experience in Generative AI and LLM systems, including agentic systems and their reliability characteristics.
Demonstrated ability to define evaluation methodology for problems without established metrics, and to negotiate quality bars that survive customer validation and regulatory review.
Experience operating as a senior technical advisor to executive stakeholders, with the presence to disagree with an executive and retain credibility.
Evidence of technical work adopted beyond your own engagements: reference architectures, methodologies, processes, or tooling used by others.
Experience mentoring technical individual contributors and raising the standard of a team.
Clear technical communication and problem-solving when requirements are unknown, including stating what is not yet known and how it would be determined.
Deep domain expertise in financial services, healthcare/life sciences, or consumer verticals.

Recognized externally in your domain: conference speaking, published technical writing, industry forums, or customer advisory participation.
Experience with domain compliance requirements: model risk management and fair lending (FSI), HIPAA, clinical safety and validated systems (HCLS), or high-volume quality and unit-economics measurement (Consumer).
Background in forward-deployed engineering or shipping production ML systems.
Experience creating large-scale evaluation datasets alongside domain experts.
Experience building or scaling a solutions architecture practice, playbook, or vertical from an early stage.

In this highly visible role, you will lead the design, architecture, implementation, lifecycle management, and advanced support of business LAN environments across complex industrial sites, with strong emphasis on Layer 1 physical infrastructure, Layer 2 switching services, and practical Layer 3 integration. You will work on meaningful infrastructure challenges that directly support safe, reliable refinery operations while partnering with site IT, enterprise network engineering, cybersecurity, facilities, telecom providers, contractors, vendors, and business stakeholders. This opportunity is ideal for a hands-on technical leader who wants to make a measurable impact in a collaborative, safety-focused organization that values integrity, inclusion, continuous improvement, and excellence. The successful candidate will influence LAN strategy and standards, strengthen resiliency, improve documentation and troubleshooting practices, mentor engineers, and drive outcomes in reliability, deployment speed, cost optimization, and operational risk reduction. If you enjoy solving complex problems, leading through influence, and building infrastructure that supports critical energy operations, this role offers the opportunity to contribute, grow, and make a difference at Marathon Petroleum. Key Responsibilities Lead the architecture, design, implementation, and lifecycle management of refinery business LAN infrastructure, including switching, structured cabling, fiber, network closets, telecom spaces, and related Layer 1 and Layer 2 components. Develop and maintain LAN standards, reference designs, configuration baselines, cabling and labeling practices, resiliency patterns, and site implementation guidance. Serve as a senior escalation point for complex LAN incidents, recurring reliability issues, performance concerns, design gaps, and high-impact outages affecting refinery business operations. Troubleshoot and resolve Layer 1 and Layer 2 issues involving cabling, fiber, optics, patching, switch stacks, VLANs, trunks, spanning tree, link aggregation, port security, and access-layer performance. Support Layer 3 integration with routed uplinks, gateways, subnet coordination, DHCP relay, firewall interfaces, wireless connectivity, and enterprise routing handoffs. Lead LAN refreshes, lifecycle replacements, business expansion projects, construction support, office moves, turnaround planning, and remediation of aging infrastructure. Partner with cybersecurity teams to strengthen segmentation, secure switch management, NAC or 802.1X readiness, logging, vulnerability remediation, and configuration compliance. Maintain accurate technical documentation, including logical and physical diagrams, switchport records, patch panel mappings, fiber routes, VLAN assignments, inventories, rack elevations, and design decisions. Coordinate changes with refinery operations, facilities, vendors, contractors, telecom providers, cybersecurity, enterprise network teams, and business stakeholders to minimize operational disruption. Set monitoring thresholds, analyze traffic and utilization trends, tune performance, identify root causes, and proactively reduce recurring network issues. Evaluate network hardware, platforms, tools, and emerging technologies to improve reliability, scalability, security, and operational efficiency. Provide technical leadership, mentoring, peer review, and guidance to engineers, site IT staff, contractors, and project teams while reinforcing safety, change control, cybersecurity, and operational risk management practices. Deploys complex network configurations for on-premise or cloud-based networks and assists in the development of playbooks for network systems. Assists in the integration of new systems and tools. Develops and maintains scripts to facilitate network administrative tasks and automate repetitive processes. Sets the requirements and thresholds for monitoring systems for network devices. Participates in troubleshooting sessions for network-related issues at all layers of the OSI model. Monitors performance, identifies areas for improvement for the network and implements performance tuning. Identifies trends in issues and determines the root cause to reduce future issues. Adheres to network policies, standards, and standard operating procedures for how-to documents. Undertakes the regular analysis and interpretation of traffic and utilization of services on network connections. Observes systems for network alerts and events so quick response can be provided and issues can be proactively addressed. Analyzes alternative hardware, platforms and technologies for the network infrastructure. Education and Experience Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, related field, or equivalent experience. 5 or more years of relevant network engineer experience required. Deep expertise in Layer 1 infrastructure, including structured cabling, copper and fiber standards, patch panels, optics, transceivers, rack layouts, cable management, labeling, testing, fiber troubleshooting, and related documentation required. Advanced Layer 2 switching expertise, including VLANs, trunks, spanning tree, loop prevention, link aggregation, switch stacking, port security, access-layer resiliency, and enterprise switching design required. Experience designing and documenting LAN architectures for large or complex environments, including standards, diagrams, refresh plans, resiliency models, implementation roadmaps, and lifecycle strategies required. Hands-on experience with enterprise switching platforms such as Cisco, Arista, or similar technologies required. Proven ability to lead network projects, hardware refreshes, outage planning, vendor coordination, construction support, office moves, and safe cutovers in active operational environments required. Demonstrated technical leadership, including mentoring, escalation support, standards development, peer review, stakeholder communication, and influence across cross-functional teams required. Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain technical risks, options, constraints, and recommendations to technical and non-technical audiences required. Preferred: Strong working knowledge of Layer 3 integration for LAN environments, including subnetting, gateways, DHCP relay, routed uplinks, routing handoffs, firewall and wireless connectivity, and escalation boundaries. Preferred: experience with regulated, refinery, industrial, or other uptime-sensitive environments; LAN cybersecurity controls such as 802.1X, NAC, secure management, port security, configuration compliance, and vulnerability remediation. Preferred: experience with network monitoring, configuration backup, log review, packet analysis, cable certification, OTDR interpretation, automation or scripting, and recurring-issue trend analysis. Preferred: CCNP, CCNA, BICSI, FOA, CompTIA Network+, Security+, or equivalent network, cabling, fiber, or cybersecurity certification. Cost Optimization – The process to analyze, plan and manage costs for cost efficiency and expense reduction, while maximizing business value. ITSM aims to align the delivery of IT services with the needs of the business and ensure that IT services are delivered efficiently, effectively, and in a way that adds value to the organization. Network Automation – Automating the configuration and management of network resources in LAN and WAN environments. This ensures consistency and scalability of the network. Network Design – Provided network design, bandwidth allocation, IP address allocation, supervising installation, configuration and maintenance on major network technologies. Network Engineering – The process of orchestrating network traffic and data flow across the enterprise ecosystem. Network Installations – Configure network hardware and software components according to organizational guidelines and technical requirements. This includes the implementation and configuration of multiple servers, network devices and network management tools as well as the management of user network access to ensure stable and reliable network operations. Network Management System – The use of network monitoring to determine, in real time, whether a network is running optimally, to optimize and improve the average percentage of time during which the network is performing its intended function. Network Security Management – The process of providing complete visibility into the network and generating data for assets (asset groupings and classifications), firewalls, applications, ports, protocols, VPNs, NAT, and security policies and vendor devices. Network Standards – Sets and establishes rules that determine how data is transmitted between different devices in the same network. Requirements Management – The process of documenting, analyzing, tracing, prioritizing and agreeing on requirements and then controlling change while also communicating to relevant stakeholders. Results Driven – Drives operational and process excellence and innovative behavior by empowering others, collaborating, taking appropriate risk, making timely decisions and holding people accountable for results. Strategic Outlook – Examines issues, generates ideas, creates future scenarios and develops plans with a long-term perspective.
